Declare an independent level for cross-classification

Source: R/levels.R
declare_level.Rd

Creates N rows as a standalone data frame registered for use by cross_levels or link_levels. Unlike add_level, a declare_level call does not nest into any existing hierarchy: it starts fresh. Use this when you need two independent populations to cross (e.g., countries and years for panel data).

Usage

declare_level(N, ...)

Arguments

N

Number of rows to create.

...

Column expressions evaluated sequentially. N is available as a scalar integer.

Value

A fabricatr_level object, meaningful only as a named argument to fabricate. It builds N rows and an ID column named after the argument it is assigned to, and holds them aside: the rows reach the fabricated frame only when a later cross_levels or link_levels names this level in .by. Declaring a level that nothing crosses or links contributes nothing to the result.

Examples

fabricate(
  countries = declare_level(N = 20, gdp = runif(N, 1, 10)),
  years     = declare_level(N = 10, shock = runif(N, 1, 5)),
  obs       = cross_levels(
    .by = c("countries", "years"),
    GDP_it = gdp + shock
  )
)
#> # A tibble: 200 × 6
#>    countries   gdp years shock obs   GDP_it
#>    <chr>     <dbl> <chr> <dbl> <chr>  <dbl>
#>  1 01         4.90 01     1.45 001     6.34
#>  2 02         7.85 01     1.45 002     9.30
#>  3 03         3.64 01     1.45 003     5.09
#>  4 04         1.97 01     1.45 004     3.41
#>  5 05         1.66 01     1.45 005     3.10
#>  6 06         4.21 01     1.45 006     5.65
#>  7 07         6.14 01     1.45 007     7.59
#>  8 08         7.10 01     1.45 008     8.55
#>  9 09         7.22 01     1.45 009     8.66
#> 10 10         4.36 01     1.45 010     5.81
#> # ℹ 190 more rows
